- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, overestimate the peak and underreact to subsequent volatility — correct by adding 5–10% buffer to early forecast spikes.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 3–5% relative to recent high.
- After a sharp spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is positive, model underestimates downside — add 2–5% downward bias to forecast mean.
- If event count is high and sentiment is mixed, model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from mean of last 10 days, apply mean reversion: adjust forecast toward 10-day moving average with decay factor 0.8.
- When bullish sentiment is high and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate price — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and supply net is positive, model underestimates volatility — add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast range.
